```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Price headroom: A's sourced self-serve comparables run from $9.99 to $499 per month per platform (not.bot, useHUMA). B is capped at $1–4 per month per individual, anchored to Maskwire's $3 bundle. With one person and a 90-day window, a single B2B customer at A's price points is worth far more than a B2C subscriber at B's.",
    "B's feature is fully commoditized: at least five live competitors already ship it, and three of them (addy.io, SimpleLogin, ProxiedMail) include it on free or near-free tiers. A free open-source Thunderbird extension already covers the client-side case, which is the very build path B's 'case for' proposes.",
    "A's competition is also crowded, but it is priced, tiered and growing in scope (for example, useHUMA's 'Agent Shield' AI-agent detection). That signals platforms are paying for this category now. B's competitors include the target feature only as a bundled extra.",
    "A's demand evidence ties the pain to direct financial loss: a $243K deepfake wire and money sent to bot dating profiles. That gives a platform a budget reason to pay. B's evidence shows annoyance with mail-client defaults, not money at stake.",
    "A has serious problems: banks need 6–18 months plus SOC 2, Zoom is already taken by World ID, and biometric regulatory risk (BIPA, GDPR) is real. These are survivable only if A narrows to small marketplaces, dating apps and review sites via self-serve, which the brief itself flags as the reachable version. B has no comparable narrowing that escapes free incumbents."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence is a set of support-forum complaints from Zoho, Apple Mail and Outlook users. They appear to be mostly business or domain-alias users hitting client defaults, not the privacy-conscious prosumers with many aliases named as the payer. None of the quotes shows willingness to pay for a standalone fix. The brief's claim of an 'underserved segment' is inferred from these complaints and is contradicted by its own list of five competitors already solving the problem, several for free.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate to low confidence. Both briefs argue persuasively against themselves. A's enterprise path is effectively closed within 90 days. Its demand quotes include a vendor executive's marketing statement, and none show a small platform committing to pay. A wins mainly on price headroom and B2B budget rationale, not on direct proof that a niche self-serve buyer exists. If A cannot avoid biometric signals, its regulatory exposure could outweigh that advantage."
}
```
